status_note: The durable-extinction endpoint was inspected during feasibility/design on 2026-09-29 before this contract was committed. This analysis is therefore exploratory and must not be described as preregistered, pre-outcome, or confirmatory. The frozen specification exists to make the exploratory result reproducible and to prevent further outcome-contingent tuning.
question: During the Palmer Adélie decline, do durable colony-code extinctions occur preferentially from smaller breeding groups, beyond shared island-year exposure and beyond the zero attrition expected under simple proportional thinning?

candidate_processes: greater edge exposure and predation risk in small breeding groups
loss of social facilitation or other positive density dependence
local breeding-habitat quality correlated with colony size
biological_motivation.identification_boundary: The census alone cannot distinguish these mechanisms. A small-group-first pattern is treated as a mechanism-generating observation, not as proof of predation, social facilitation, snow, or terrain effects.

primary.reason: These are the three stable-roster islands already used by the pre-existing breeding-patch concentration analysis; this restriction avoids interpreting colony-code roster changes as biological extinction.

sensitivity.rule: Retain the same event definition and require continuous future observation of each colony code; transitions with an active code missing at t+1 are excluded from the proportional-thinning diagnostic.

risk_set.entry: A colony code enters a one-year risk interval only when its breeding-pair count is >0 at year t and the same code is observed at adjacent year t+1.

event.name: durable_extinction
event.definition: count at t+1 equals zero, the colony code is continuously observed in every later island census year through the dataset endpoint, and every later observed count remains zero

matched_hazard.predictor: z(log1p breeding pairs at t), standardized across informative risk rows within the analysis scope
matched_hazard.conditioning: exact conditional logistic likelihood within island x start-year strata
matched_hazard.informative_stratum: contains at least one durable-extinction event and at least one survivor

permutation.scheme: Within each informative island-year stratum, hold the observed number of events fixed and randomize which risk-set members receive the event label.
permutation.statistic: sum of standardized log1p breeding-pair size among event colonies

matched_hazard.size_share_identifiability: Because island total is fixed inside an island-year stratum, absolute group size and within-island share encode nearly the same ordering. They are not entered simultaneously as independent causal predictors. Share is descriptive only.

proportional_thinning_diagnostic.purpose: Test whether one-year zero attrition is far more frequent than expected if the observed next-year breeding-pair mass were allocated proportionally to current colony-code shares.
proportional_thinning_diagnostic.simulation: For each eligible island-year transition, retain the observed next-year breeding-pair mass assigned to codes active at t and allocate it multinomially among those codes in proportion to their t shares. Mass in new or reappearing codes is conditioned out rather than reassigned.
proportional_thinning_diagnostic.statistic: total number of active-at-t colony codes receiving zero at t+1
proportional_thinning_diagnostic.boundary: This is a one-step allocation null, not a full demographic process model and not a direct model of durable extinction.

exploratory_readout.ordered_small_group_attrition_flag: true only when the primary stable-roster matched hazard has a negative size coefficient with randomization p <= 0.05 and the primary proportional-thinning diagnostic has more observed zeros than its 97.5% null quantile with upper-tail p <= 0.05
exploratory_readout.interpretation: A positive flag motivates independent mechanism tests; it does not convert this post-outcome analysis into confirmatory evidence.

prohibited_claims: Small colony size causally causes extinction.
Skua predation caused the observed attrition.
Social facilitation or an Allee effect has been identified from these census data.
Snow or terrain has been shown to drive colony-code extinction.
colony_code is equivalent to a mapped physical subcolony polygon.
This analysis was preregistered or frozen before the extinction outcome was inspected.
next_prospective_gates: Resolve chick-census duplicate-key semantics without using num_chicks, then freeze a chick-production validation before opening the chick outcome.
Freeze a species x terrain life-history test before joining terrain predictors to demographic outcomes.
